//: Exemptions for the access-gate scanner. Every entry needs a path, a category and a
reason, and an entry that matches nothing fails the scan: an allowlist nobody prunes
is how a check becomes a formality.
Categories: 'contract' (the policy that defines what a gate is), 'tests' (a test must
be able to name the gate it plants), 'documentation' (licence text and voluntary
support links the project ships), 'third-party' (another party's paid capability,
which is read and respected rather than bypassed).
Prefer 'tokens' when only some tokens are legitimate in a file. A whole-file exemption
for the feature catalog would stop the scanner from noticing a gated feature id added
to the one file that declares every feature.

allow.reason: The scanner and its self-test necessarily spell the tokens they detect, and the self-test plants violations on purpose in a temporary tree.
Defines the contract: it lists the legacy entitlement keys the migration removes and the gate tokens the audit detects. A policy that forbids a word has to be able to spell it.
A test that proves an internal gate cannot exist has to name the token it plants, and the platform contract test names the audit it calls.
Rewrites the GPL licence notice the About screen shows during the product-identity migration. It writes licence text and touches no feature access.
The licence name and text the About screen shows, and the voluntary Ko-fi support links. Neither unlocks anything: the app is GPL-3.0 and every feature is reachable without supporting the project.
Renders the licence terms and the support links; carries no feature entitlement.
Reads WhatsApp's own presence-subscription protocol vocabulary from the installed client. This is another party's server-side concept, not a WA X feature gate.
Names NoPaywallContractTest as the test that covers the access contract. Only that token is exempt: a gated feature id added to the catalog still fails the scan.
